answer: I would like to talk about someone I see every single day. The family member I am closest to is my younger sister, despite the fact that we argue like any siblings do. She is a few years younger than me and still a student, and she is easily the most hard-working person in our house. In many ways she feels more like a friend than a sibling. We share almost everything, from silly jokes to serious worries, and she is the first person I turn to when something is bothering me. What makes our bond so strong is that we are [[brutally honest]] with each other, even when the truth is uncomfortable. As for what we do together, we enjoy simple things, like watching films, walking along the Jamuna in the evening, or just talking late into the night over cups of tea. Sometimes I help her with her English, and in return she tells me when my ideas are ridiculous. She has this ability to make me laugh no matter how [[miserable]] I am feeling, which is a real gift, especially after a long, tiring day at work. I think the reason we get along so well is that siblings who grow up together develop an almost [[intuitive]] understanding of one another. We can often tell what the other is thinking from a single look across the dinner table. Honestly, I feel incredibly [[fortunate]] to have her, because not everyone is lucky enough to be close to their family.

followUps.q: Do you think you will stay close as you get older?
followUps.answer: I really hope so. She may move away for work or marriage one day, but I think our bond is strong enough to survive the distance, just as it has with my elder sister.

followUps.q: Do you ever argue with her?
followUps.answer: Of course, usually about trivial things like the television remote. But our arguments never last long, and by dinner time we have normally forgotten what we were [[squabbling]] about in the first place.
